sections.html:
Pocatello is the home of Idaho State University, in the Portneuf Valley of southeastern Idaho. Population was an estimated 58,771 on July 1, 2025, up only 3.6 percent from April 2020, so demand here moves at a steadier pace than in the Treasure Valley or North Idaho.

Homes are modestly priced. Owner-occupied units had a median value of $271,000 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and 64.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $948. A citywide median says little about one house, so yours may be worth more or less.

Older houses near the old rail corridor and homes close to the Portneuf River each raise their own questions about condition, noise and drainage. Be ready to talk about both if either describes your property.

Pocatello took in the neighboring city of Alameda in 1962. Chubbuck, to the north, turned down a similar merger and is still a separate city, so a Chubbuck address follows that city's rules and not Pocatello's.

Part of Pocatello reaches into Power County, where the school district is American Falls Joint School District 381 and not the Pocatello Chubbuck district. Confirm which jurisdiction your parcel falls in before you gather permit or tax information.

Pocatello has hot summers and sharp winters. The record high is 104 degrees, and the record low is minus 33 degrees on February 1, 1985. The city building department uses a 3 foot frost level for foundation design, a clue to how deep the ground freezes. Frost heave can crack slabs, shift garage floors and open gaps at foundation edges.

  • Walk the foundation and look for diagonal cracks or doors that stick.
  • Check the garage slab and exterior concrete for lifting.
  • Inspect the roof after heavy snow years, and note the date of any repair.

Buyers ask about foundation and roof early. A cash buyer prices them in and does not require you to repair them first.

The Bannock County part of Pocatello is in the Pocatello Chubbuck School District 25, which runs three public high schools, four public middle schools and thirteen public elementary schools. Two public charter schools and several private schools add choices.

Pocatello Regional Airport has commercial air service. Pocatello Regional Transit runs buses on five hourly routes Monday to Saturday, with no evening or Sunday service.

The Building Department enforces codes for new construction and remodeling and handles abatement of dangerous buildings. Apply through the city's eTRAKiT online portal, or call 208-234-6158. The code follows the International Building Code and International Residential Code with local amendments, and permit fees are published each fiscal year.

  • Ask whether past work on your house was permitted, since a buyer's inspector may ask.
  • If a dangerous building notice is on the property, tell us at the start, because it limits what a buyer can do.
  • Keep contractor receipts for the roof, furnace and water heater, which show the age of major systems.

The county mails bills by the fourth Monday in November. The first half or the full year is due December 20, and the second half is due June 20 of the following year. Either date moves to the next business day when it lands on a weekend.

Interest on a late second half is figured at 1 percent per month back to January 1, so a payment a few days late can carry about six months of interest. Bills for new construction and occupancy sit on a separate roll, mailed in January and due in February.

The Board of Equalization decides whether market value is fair and accurate. It cannot lower a value because the tax is hard to pay. The treasurer is in Room 203 of the Bannock County Courthouse, 624 E. Center St., phone 208-236-7260, and the county's Property Tax Hub explains each step.

Under Idaho Code section 55-2501 and the sections after it, sellers of one to four unit residential property complete a property condition disclosure form. You describe known defects on it whether you list the house or sell for cash. Idaho Code 55-2508 gives the standard form.

Cash suits an owner facing a repair bill, an inherited house in another town, or a tenant problem. A listing may suit a house in good condition. We buy as-is and make an offer once we have the details. You owe nothing if you say no, and we do not promise a price before we see the property.

The path is short. You share the address, repairs and any tenant or lien details. We make an offer. If you accept, a title company handles the closing, pays off any mortgage or unpaid taxes from the proceeds and gives you the rest.

Before you call, gather your latest Bannock County tax bill, any permit records and a list of the repairs you know about. If part of your parcel is in Power County, mention it so the right office is checked.

faqs.q: When are Bannock County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay the full year or the first half by December 20, and the second half by June 20. A weekend due date moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Pocatello property assessment?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday in June, to the Bannock County Board of Equalization. Notices are mailed the first Monday in June.

faqs.q: Is all of Pocatello in Bannock County?
faqs.a: Most of it is, but part reaches into Power County. That part is served by American Falls Joint School District 381, so check your parcel before gathering tax and school information.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Pocatello house if it needs foundation or roof work?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy as-is, so the foundation and roof can stay unrepaired. You still complete Idaho's seller disclosure form and describe the problems you know about.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Pocatello?
faqs.a: $271,000 for owner-occupied units in 2020 to 2024. That is a citywide estimate, so your own house may be worth more or less.
